verdicts.rationale: Verified by code trace. useReports.ts:407-416 registers ONLY a `virgil-anchor-orphaned` (Mode-B) listener — there is no `virgil-textobject-orphaned` (Mode-A block-removal) listener anywhere in the hook (grep over the file confirms a single addEventListener at :414). The sibling Mode-A sweep that useReports lacks exists in useTodos.ts:226-243 (removeTextObjectLink on the dispatched uuid) and useArchive.ts:131. TextObjectOrphanGuard (linked-anchor.ts:162-187) dispatches the event per removed block, and its own doc-comment at linked-anchor.ts:148 explicitly names `useReports` as an intended consumer — so the contract says useReports should listen and it doesn't. MarginaliaAnchorGuard early-returns on LIFECYCLE_DELETE_META (linked-anchor.ts:246-248), so the Archive/Delete drag-handle path really does let the block go without resurrection. The stale uuid then survives in links[].textObjectIds, so getLinkedTextObjectIds(c).length>0 stays true and ReportsPanel.tsx:101 keeps the jump chevron wired; jumpToCard returns false silently (links.ts:619) when resolveLink finds no surviving uuid (links.ts:470-487). The gutter marker (EditorPane.tsx:1786-1808) emits per pid but Marginalia can't place a marker on a removed block, so the gutter marker vanishes while the panel jump button persists — exactly the surface disagreement claimed. MEDIUM is correct: a stuck dead-jump button + omni/panel divergence, no content loss, recoverable by deleting the card.
verdicts.correctedRootCause: The deeper cause is a broken contract, not just a missing listener: linked-anchor.ts:148 enumerates `useTodos / useReports / useExamples / useArchive` as the four Mode-A orphan consumers, but only useTodos and useArchive ever registered the `virgil-textobject-orphaned` handler. useReports.ts:407 and useNotes.ts:207 both register ONLY the Mode-B `virgil-anchor-orphaned` event. The orphan event is fanned out by TextObjectOrphanGuard.appendTransaction (linked-anchor.ts:169-183) on diff.removedBlocks.
verdicts.class: Mode-A-anchorable card hooks that omit the `virgil-textobject-orphaned` listener while still recording Mode-A textObjectIds. Confirmed siblings: useNotes.ts (only :207 virgil-anchor-orphaned, no textobject sweep) — same defect for notes' Mode-A links, equal severity. useTodos + useArchive are correct; useReports + useNotes diverge.

verdicts.rationale: The core claim is CONFIRMED but the worst-case symptom is overstated. Verified: linkedAnchor is app-state stripped on .tex export and must be re-stamped on load (linked-anchor.ts:9-13). EditorLayout.tsx applyLinkedAnchors restore loop (:3265-3306) builds records from notes/todoItems/comments/cutterCards/highlights ONLY; reports/report-requests are absent, and the effect dep array (:3312) likewise omits reports. `report` AND `report-request` are valid LinkedAnchorKind values (links.ts:721-729) and the drag-handle 'report' gesture with wantRangeAnchor does mint a Mode-B mark via createAnchor(ed,'report-request') + updateLinkedAnchorCard (drag-handle-actions.ts:412-428), so a report-request legitimately carries a Mode-B mark that the restore loop never re-applies → the in-text tint disappears on reload. The todo-mode-b-reconciler.test.tsx:372-378 comment enshrines exactly this fix for todos ('note/highlight/cutter/revision ARE in that loop') and describes the identical symptom (tint vanishes, jump degrades to paragraph). HOWEVER, the finder's 'lose all resolution' sub-case is essentially unreachable: the drag-handle path ALWAYS sets paragraphId (drag-handle-actions.ts:230-236) and passes it to createReportRequest → addReportRequest(paragraphId,...) → addTextObjectLink (useReports.ts:180-181), so every Mode-B report also carries a Mode-A textObjectId, and resolveLink falls back to the paragraph (links.ts:470-486). So the realistic symptom is: lost in-text tint + jump degrades to paragraph-level. No data/content loss. MEDIUM stands (it matches the todos precedent and is a genuine reload-persistence regression of an intentional UX affordance), but reclassified to correct the 'no resolution' overclaim.
verdicts.correctedRootCause: Same root cause as the finder (reports omitted from EditorLayout.tsx:3265-3306 applyLinkedAnchors restore loop + the :3312 dep array), but the impact ceiling is paragraph-level degradation + lost tint, NOT total resolution loss, because the drag-handle always co-records a Mode-A paragraphId (drag-handle-actions.ts:230-236 → useReports.ts:180-181). An anchor-only report (null paragraphId) has no UI producer.
verdicts.class: Any Mode-B-capable card kind omitted from the EditorLayout.tsx:3265-3306 restore loop. Reports/report-requests are the omitted pair; no other newer Mode-B kind currently exists in the loop's blind spot (examples are derived-block, not Mode-B range-anchored).

verdicts.rationale: CONFIRMED as a real silent loss of user-entered content, and UPGRADED from MEDIUM. isAutoTitle (panel-registry.ts:254-258) returns true for any title matching `^<Label> \d+$` where Label = CARD_TITLE_LABELS[kind]; report's titleLabel is 'Report' (card-registry.tsx:394-396), so isAutoTitle('report','Report 8') === true — pinned by auto-title.test.ts:59. migrateReportRecord (useReports.ts:55-59) runs on EVERY load and nulls title to '' whenever isAutoTitle is true, with no way to distinguish a deliberately-typed title of the same shape. The report card has a user-editable title field (updateReportTitle, useReports.ts:205-216; ReportsPanel wires onUpdateReportTitle), so a user can absolutely type 'Report 8' (a natural name for a numbered report series), and it is silently discarded on the next reload with no warning. Per the severity rubric, silent loss of user content (the rubric lists 'lost title/author' under DATA-LOSS) — I upgrade to HIGH: it is a silent, no-warning loss on a routine action (reload), enshrined by a test. Not full DATA-LOSS only because the lost field is a short title (not the report body) and is re-typable.
verdicts.correctedRootCause: isAutoTitle is purely shape-based (panel-registry.ts:258 regex) and cannot distinguish a stale generated title from a deliberate user title of the same shape. The BUG #31 fix stopped PERSISTING generated titles (useReports.ts:147 forces title:'' on create) but left the load-time stripper (useReports.ts:57) running on all titles, so any user title matching `^Report \d+$` is collateral.
verdicts.class: Every auto-titling kind whose titleLabel yields a human-plausible '<Label> N' title and that strips on load via isAutoTitle: report ('Report 8'), example ('Example 4' — most likely to be human-numbered), note ('Note 3'), todo ('Task 5'), footnote ('Footnote 1'), archive ('Archive Text 1'). All run isAutoTitle in their migrate*Record. Reports and examples are the highest-risk because users number them as a series. auto-title.test.ts:51-64 enshrines the false-positive across note/footnote/archive/todo/report/example.

verdicts.rationale: Verified end-to-end. requestToReport (morphs/index.ts:149-161) emits a report with no aiRequest field — the flag is dropped. The morph path EditorPane.tsx:863-918 convertCardWithRemap, case 'report-request' (:903-905), calls reportsHookRaw.convertCard(id,'report') and never calls bridgeCardAiRequestFlag(...,false). useReports.convertCard (:267-279) just runs applyCardMorph inside update() — a pure data flip, no inbox side effect (contrast setRequestAiRequest at :246-258 which DOES bridge). The inbox entry is matched by linkedTo.cardId (ai-request-bridge.ts:94-103) and only removed on a value=false toggle (:132-134), which never fires on morph. CARD_REGISTRY confirms report-request's aiRequest routing emits kind:'report'/linkPanel:'reports' (card-registry.tsx:422) while the `report` kind has NO aiRequest routing (card-registry.tsx:394-414) — so the morphed report has no checkbox to issue the false-toggle. The entry stays status:'pending' forever, unreachable from the now-flagless report card; a /editor/answer-report-request drain would act on a stale request. MEDIUM is correct: no content loss, but an orphaned-pending inbox entry + a stale skill-drain target. The lossy confirm (EditorPane.tsx:874-876) warns about 'title and byline' but not the abandoned AI request — a secondary correct nit.
verdicts.correctedRootCause: The morph chokepoint (EditorPane.tsx:863-918) never reconciles the AI-request inbox: it remaps the float key (:915) but does not bridge a dropped aiRequest flag. The owning hook's convertCard (useReports.ts:267) is a pure morph with no side effect, so the bridge is nobody's responsibility on the morph path.
verdicts.class: Every morph whose source kind carries an aiRequest flag the target kind drops, with no bridge-clear in the morph path. cutter-comment→suggestion and revision-comment→suggestion route through the same un-bridged convertCardWithRemap. note→highlight CARRIES aiRequest across (morphs/index.ts:183) so highlight inherits it but highlight also has no toggle UI (card-registry.tsx:206 routing exists, no checkbox) — verify highlight's inbox reachability. The A9 morph chokepoint reconciles float keys but never the AI-request inbox for any pair.

verdicts.rationale: CONFIRMED as a real omission but DOWNGRADED from MEDIUM. Verified: ReportsPanel.tsx:68-126 invokes CardListPanel with count but NO aiRequests/onUpdateAiRequestText/onDeleteAiRequest props, and ReportsHost (reports-host.tsx:29-65) never calls useAiRequestsContext nor forwards aiRequests — contrast footnotes-host.tsx:30,48-50 which reads the context and threads it, and FootnotePanel.tsx:68-70 which filters r.kind==='footnote'. CardListPanel only renders its pending-requests section when aiRequests is non-empty (CardListPanel.tsx:96-98), so the section is structurally absent for reports. ai-requests.tsx:6-11 explicitly names FIVE panels (notes, footnotes, todo, reports, citations) as AI-request hosts and 'report' is a first-class AiRequestKind drained by /editor/answer-report-request — so reports IS the documented gap. HOWEVER, downgraded to LOW because the realistic user-facing impact is small: the ONLY in-app producer of a kind:'report' request is the report-request card's own aiRequest checkbox (setRequestAiRequest → bridge), and that card is itself visible in the docked panel with its flag checked. There is no can-I-request / standalone path that files a card-less kind:'report' request from the UI (grep confirms no such producer). So the missing 'Pending AI requests (N)' section only matters for card-less entries written by a skill/external tool — an edge path. The queued request is not invisible in the normal flow; it surfaces as its own card. Real contract violation, low practical impact, no data loss.
verdicts.correctedRootCause: Two-seam omission (host forgot useAiRequestsContext + panel has no aiRequests prop / no r.kind filter), same as the finder. The downgrade rests on the fact that the report-request card is the sole producer and is itself panel-visible, so the missing section is redundant in the dominant flow rather than the only surface.
verdicts.class: Any AI-request-bearing panel that forgets to thread aiRequests through host+panel. Reports is the only one of the five named in ai-requests.tsx that omits it; the other four (notes/footnotes/todo/citations) wire it. Verify citations actually filters (CitationsPanel is in the r.kind=== grep hit-list, so it does).
